title: GPA Calculator - 4.0 Scale Cumulative & Semester GPA
description: Calculate high school and college GPA on a 4.0 scale with plus/minus toggles, credit hour weights, and multi-semester cumulative tracking.
quickAnswer: GPA (Grade Point Average) on a standard 4.0 scale is calculated by multiplying each course grade's point value (e.g. A = 4.0, B = 3.0) by its course credit hours to obtain grade points, summing all grade points, and dividing by the total completed credit hours: GPA = Total Grade Points ÷ Total Credit Hours. Pass/fail classes and withdrawn credits are excluded.

formula.title: GPA Formula
formula.explanation: Multiply each class's grade point (A = 4.0, B = 3.0, C = 2.0, D = 1.0, F = 0.0) by its course credit hours to get grade points, sum the points for all courses, and divide by the total credit hours.

commonMistakes.title: Averaging Letter Grades Without Credit Weights
commonMistakes.description: Giving equal weight to a 4-credit organic chemistry course and a 1-credit seminar will give an inaccurate GPA. Always multiply each course by its credit hours.

commonMistakes.title: Averaging Semester GPAs Directly
commonMistakes.description: You cannot take the simple average of two semester GPAs unless both terms had the exact same number of completed credit hours. Always sum total grade points and divide by total credits.

commonMistakes.title: Assuming All Schools Use 4.0 Unweighted
commonMistakes.description: Many secondary schools use 5.0 scales for Honors/AP classes, and some colleges don't distinguish plus and minus grades. Use the toggle above to match your institution's policy.

faqs.q: How is GPA calculated on a 4.0 scale?
faqs.a: GPA is calculated by multiplying each course's grade point value by its credit hours to find total grade points, summing those points across all classes, and dividing by total earned credit hours: GPA = Total Grade Points ÷ Total Credit Hours.

faqs.q: What are the standard 4.0 scale grade points with plus and minus?
Do all colleges and high schools use the same grading scale?
faqs.a: No. Grading scales vary significantly by institution. Some universities award 4.33 points for an A+, while others cap all A grades at 4.00 or do not use plus/minus distinctions at all. High schools often use weighted 5.0 scales for Honors and Advanced Placement (AP) coursework. Always verify with your institution's official registrar.

faqs.q: How do credit hours affect my GPA?
faqs.a: Credit hours act as mathematical multipliers. A 4-credit lab science or calculus course has twice the impact on your GPA as a 2-credit elective course. Earning an A in a 4-credit course provides 16 grade points, whereas an A in a 2-credit course provides 8 points.

faqs.q: How do I calculate cumulative GPA from past semesters?
faqs.a: Multiply your previous cumulative GPA by previous completed credit hours to find prior points. Add your new semester points, then divide by the new total credit hours: Cumulative GPA = (Prior Points + New Semester Points) ÷ (Prior Credits + New Credits).

faqs.q: Do Pass/Fail or Withdrawn (W) courses impact GPA?
faqs.a: Standard Pass/Fail, Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory, and Withdrawn (W) notations do not carry grade points and are excluded from both total points and total GPA credit denominators.

faqs.q: Is my personal transcript or GPA information stored?
faqs.a: Never. All calculations run strictly client-side inside your browser memory. We do not store, track, or transmit any student data, course names, or grades.
